places.name: 23 Sutton Court Road, Plaistow
places.coordinateMethod: OpenStreetMap Nominatim search on 23 November 2026, source osm-nominatim-2026. Query: 23 Sutton Court Road, Plaistow, London, UK
places.standsTodaySource: Left unknown. Street View on 24 November 2026 (capture Sep 2025), labelled 24 Sutton Court Road, shows a brick terrace still there, but the door numbers were not read and the picture cannot say whether number 23 is the 1911 house. Bomb Sight (bombsight.org) was in maintenance on 24 November 2026 and drew no bomb markers, so it does not say whether a bomb fell on this house on 19 April 1941. The Commonwealth War Graves entry says Henry George Andrews died at 23 Sutton Court Road that day, not whether the house was destroyed or repaired. PlanIndex's reading of Newham application 26/01578/HH, granted 11 November 2026, is a householder rear extension at 23 Sutton Court Road, E13 9NN, which means a house is at that address now. The council's own documents were not opened. None of this chooses standing over rebuilt.
places.significance: 23 Sutton Court Road, Plaistow is on the site for William Cousins, Amelia Cousins, Henry George Andrews, Rosina Maud Andrews: lived 1911 to 19 April 1941.

events.summary: 1911 census, 23 Sutton Court Road, Plaistow: William Cousins, 61, widower, Assistant Dock Foreman, born Hackney, and his daughter Amelia Ann, 34. The crossed-out figures say 8 children born, 7 living. This is the house where Rosina and Henry George later lived and died.

His army papers give 23 Sutton Court Road, Plaistow, as his address when he attested in December 1915, and his wife Rosina there as his next of kin; his papers on leaving the army in 1919 give the same address.

places.blurb: The house where Rosina and Henry George lived, and where they and their son Sidney were killed on 19 April 1941.
